chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) is of divine origin. The Prophet DIZOLELE-MPUNGU WAFIDUSWA Isaac is its Visible Founder.
No other person in the whole Church (Mother Church and Extensions) may declare himself Founder.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) is apolitical.
The apolitical character of the Association does not extend to its members.
No member may therefore use it as an instrument for political ends.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The name « EGLISE BON NOUVEAU MESSAGE (KCC) », abbreviated « EBNM », derives from the revelation received by the Prophet DIZOLELE-MPUNGU WAFIDUSWA Isaac on 12 April 1958. He was then in Boma, in the Province of Kongo Central, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
This name confers on the Church its true identity and defines its vocation and its mission.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The consonants KCC constitute the prophetic and distinctive signs of the Church. The pronunciation « KASESE » of these signs must be respected and remain identical in all languages.
They must be used everywhere in gold characters, on a white background, without any overprinting.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
Notwithstanding the change of the name « Eglise Universelle de Douze Apôtres » to « Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) », the former, being covered by Ministerial Order n°JUST.GS/CAB.MIN/068/94 of 2 April 1994, remains a patrimony of the Church in accordance with Art. 8 of Law n°004/2001 of 20 July 2001 laying down the general provisions applicable to non-profit associations (ASBL) and Public Utility Establishments.
Any offender shall be liable to legal proceedings.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The name « Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) » may not be modified, either in time or in space.
It is therefore definitive.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The Spiritual Seat is a sacrosanct place of the Church, that is to say, it is sacred and kept holy.
It is the place of residence of the Spiritual Head.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: The Spiritual Seat is the ideal place where the ordinary sessions of the Assembly of the Clergy and the consecration of Apostles take place.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: Every adherent is recommended to visit the Spiritual Seat at least once in his lifetime.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: The Spiritual Seat of the Church is governed by a treaty called the « Treaty of the Spiritual Seat ».

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The contribution to the construction and modernization of the Spiritual Seat is an immediate and uninterrupted duty of every KCCISTE.
No organ whatsoever may suspend or interrupt it, either in time or in space.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: The emphyteutic lease contract of the Spiritual Seat, the archives and the museums are placed under the management of the Pontiff-Counsellor in charge of the Permanent Secretariat of the Supremacy.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The Registered and Administrative Office of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) is located in Kinshasa, at Rue Tshipepele n°8162, Quartier Salongo in the Commune of Lemba, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, in the heart of Central Africa.
In accordance with art. 3 of the statutes, the Spiritual Seat is established on Mount MATANCI, located between Makaba and Mbanza-Me-DIZOLELE, respectively the native village of the Prophet and his village of origin, Sector of Kinkenge, Territory of Luozi, in the Province of Kongo Central, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Representation Office of the Spiritual Seat in Kinshasa, called the « DIRECTION DU SIEGE » (Seat Directorate), is established at Avenue NYEMBO n°12, Quartier RIGHINI in the Commune of LEMBA. It is the Office of the Supremacy.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: The name « Direction du Siège » (Seat Directorate) is an emanation of the Spiritual Seat of the Church.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The Seat Directorate may be transferred to another location in the Democratic Republic of the Congo if:
• Working conditions are no longer decent at the place where it is located;
• A need requires the concentration of services in another, more appropriate place.
This list of grounds is not exhaustive.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: The Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) may cover a social activity that does not belong to it only subject to the express authorization of the Supremacy.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The Mothers are grouped in the « Action de la Femme de l'Eglise Bon Nouveau Message », abbreviated « AFEBNM ».
The Youth are organized within the « Jeunesse de l'Eglise Bon Nouveau Message », abbreviated « JEBNM ».
The Music of the Church is managed by the « Présidence Générale de la Musique » (General Presidency of Music), abbreviated « PGM ».
As specialized services of the Church, the three organizations carry out their activities in accordance with the purposes of the Association.
Each of these services is provided with a general framework.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
These Internal Regulations are applicable wherever the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) carries out its activities.
They govern all persons, lay or religious, professing KCCISME, regardless of race, sex and class.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: In order to avoid a disorderly establishment of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) throughout the world, any KCCISTE living in a place where the EBNM does not exist may carry out religious activities only with the written or solemn authorization of the Supremacy.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: When established in a country other than the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Church keeps the name of the EBNM. In relation to the Mother Church, it constitutes an « EXTENSION » or « BRANCH ».

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t:
The Mother Church of the DR Congo and the Extensions all depend on the Supremacy, in particular with regard to:
• The doctrine
• The statutory and regulatory foundations
• The appointment of the leaders of the clergy
• The consecration of Apostles The appointment of the leaders of the Extensions.
The submission of detailed annual reports.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: For its functioning, the Supremacy determines the participation of the Mother Church and of the Extensions.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: A Branch may neither add a doctrinal element to, nor remove, nor modify anything of the doctrine of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC).

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: Any new cultural element relating to doctrine and discipline must, before being integrated, be examined by the Supremacy.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: The Statutes of the Extensions must be modelled on those of the Mother Church.

chap: Creation, name, seat, purposes and area of activity
t: Before being submitted to the assessment of the authorities of the host country, the Statutes of the Extensions must first be examined by the Supremacy.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t:
Radical monotheism is the doctrinal basis of the Church.
No one may give teaching founded on another belief.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: The objectives of the teaching, the words of the Covenant, the Profession of faith and the Commandments of the Church must be known by every KCCISTE.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: Only the Hebrew Bible and the Prophet DIZOLELE-MPUNGU WAFIDUSWA Isaac constitute the sources of the religious teaching of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC).

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t:
Being of divine origin, the KCC - NKANDA WAMBOTE WAMPA is sacred. It may be neither diluted nor falsified.
In time as in space, it is forbidden for anyone to make any modification to it, however slight.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: In the context of the revelation, the consonants KCC constitute prophetic and distinctive signs of the Church.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: The consonants KCC and the effigy of His Eminence the Spiritual Head may be engraved on wearable insignia or on clothing fabric only with the express authorization of the Spiritual Head.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: The wearing of KCC insignia, the prophetic letters «K», which means « NKANDA » or « MESSAGE », « C » and « C » meaning respectively GOOD and NEW, is authorized for every KCCISTE.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: For an exact translation of the signs KCC, one must start from Kikongo, the language in which the Eternal presented them to the Prophet: K=Nkanda; C=Wambote; C=Wampa.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: A KCCISTE may not wear an insignia of another religion.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t:
Every KCCISTE must abstain from any foreign doctrine.
Any mixing with another doctrine entails expulsion.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: Every KCCISTE is called to protect and defend KCCISME and its doctrine, whatever the circumstances.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: The rights of printing, reproduction, dissemination and publication of KCCISME and of everything relating to it are reserved to the SUPREMACY, save with its express authorization.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: KCCISME may be revised, corrected, expanded or translated into other languages only by the hand of the Visible Founder of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC).

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: The adherent acquires the title of KCCISTE through the sacrament of the First Anointing.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: The Profession of faith forms part of the sabbath liturgy. It is declared in the local language.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: Every KCCISTE is identified everywhere by his ethics, his membership or First Anointing card and/or by the wearing of the « KCC » insignia.

chap: Content and protection of the doctrinal specificity
t: Literary and artistic works as well as ensemble hymns may be published on a material medium only with authorization issued by the Ministry of the Word and Life of the Church.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t:
The role of the member by right is:
• To inspire the Church
• To guide the management of the Church spiritually, administratively and materially;
• To serve as depositary and guarantor of the prophetic heritage.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t: The Spiritual Head, the Prophet of the Eternal, His Eminence DIZOLELE-MPUNGU WAFIDUSWA Isaac, is entitled to decent social benefits as defined by the Effective Members;

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t: The status of Member by right is neither transferable nor acquired by succession.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t:
The Entitled Member has a permanent status in the Association.
In the event of permanent incapacity of the member by right, the entitled member is appointed and removed by the Family Council of the first line of descent.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t:
The entitled member sits in the central organs of the Church and has the right to speak.
He may also sit on the Executive Committee and in the General Assembly.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t: The powers of the effective member are defined in articles 62 and 65 of the Statutes.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t: The effective member must comply with the powers conferred on him by law n°004/2001 of 20 July 2001 laying down the general provisions applicable to non-profit associations (ASBL), as detailed in Art. 64 of the Statutes of the Association.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t:
The appointment of an effective member must be notified by the Legal Representative, except for the Mother Church, where the Spiritual Head exercises this power.
In the case of a voluntary withdrawal, the effective member must send a letter to the Association.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t: The status of KCCISTE is lost through resignation, expulsion or death.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t: Any member who violates one of the clauses of Art. 56 of these regulations is expelled from the Association.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t:
The expulsion procedure for any member begins with the Parish Council, which establishes the facts and reports them to the hierarchy with supporting evidence or testimony.
The expulsion is pronounced by His Eminence the Spiritual Head.
However, if the case is proven, the Spiritual Head may pronounce the appropriate sanction without going through the Parish Council.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t:
The role of the adherent is to:
• Defend the doctrine and discipline of the Association.
• Promote the social actions of the Association.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t:
If, despite advice and exhortations, an adherent remains inactive for 6 months, he is declared a deserter.
The Parish Council establishes the desertion and rules according to whether the person is a member or a servant.

chap: Roles, rights, duties, admission, revocation, departure and expulsion of members
t: The adherent is subject to the expulsion procedure provided for in Articles 59 to 61 of these Internal Regulations.

chap: Contribution of members and third parties
t: Every member of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) has the duty to support the Church financially, materially and morally, without anything in return and without expecting reimbursement.

chap: Contribution of members and third parties
t: The financial, material or moral contribution of a member becomes definitively the patrimony of the Association.

chap: Contribution of members and third parties
t:
Any third party, natural or legal person, may freely support the Association in order to cover the purposes it has set for itself.
This support (a legacy or a gift) is not refundable.
However, the Association may record in a Golden Book the identity of the donor as well as the nature of his support.

The Organs of the EBNM are:
A. At the International level:
• The Supremacy • The Assembly of the Clergy • The General Council B. At the level of the Mother Church:
• The Assembly of Apostles • The General Assembly • The Constituent Assembly • The Executive Committee • The Provincial/Urban Council • The Provincial Committee C. At the level of the Extensions:
• The Council of Apostles • The National Committee • The Constituent Assembly • The National Executive Committee D. At the local level:
• The Parish Council;
• The Parish Committee.

The ordinary session of the various organs comprises three stages:
• The opening ceremony
• The proceedings
• The closing ceremony.
The opening ceremony comprises:
• the meditation,
• the address for the occasion and
• the official declaration of opening by the president of the organ;
The proceedings comprise:
• the roll call of participants leading to the validation of the quorum;
the constitution of the bureau:
• the presentation;
the adoption and examination of the items on the agenda.
The closing ceremony is marked by:
• the meditation;
• the reading of the final communiqué or of the summary report and
• the official declaration of closing by the president of the organ.
OFFICE NOTARIAT 4.

Only the members of the organ and persons expressly invited in writing may attend any session.
Save with the express authorization of the Spiritual Head, sessions are held behind closed doors.
All members of the bureau must be full members of the organ.
The agenda must appear in the invitation to the session.
The conduct of the sittings is governed by Internal Regulations drawn up for the occasion and adopted by the members of the organ.

Only the members of the organ have the right to vote.
Voting is by show of hands or by secret ballot.
Decisions taken at a meeting of an organ may be made public only by the President of the organ, subject to Article 31 of the Statutes.
The Supremacy is the organ resident at the Spiritual Seat which coordinates all the spiritual and material activities of both the Mother Church and the Extensions.
In addition to His Eminence the Spiritual Head, the Supremacy comprises 6 Members called Pontiff-Counsellors and one or two entitled members.
The Supremacy has the appropriate technical services at its disposal.

In addition to the offerings collected on the anniversary days of 8 March, […] April and 30 April, the Supremacy receives for its functioning a [percentage of] the proceeds of the major operations (Harvest Festival and Festival of Peaceful Gifts).
The Sovereign Pontiff exercises the powers of the Head of the Church in the event of permanent incapacity of the Spiritual Head.
The Pontiff in charge of the Minparvie is represented at the level of each country by [...] of the Word and Life of the Church;
The purpose, composition, powers and functioning of the General Council are defined in articles 44 to 47 of the Statutes.
At each session of the General Council, the president shall present in his opening speech the results of the previous financial year and the prospects for the future.

Six months before the holding of the General Council, the President notifies the members of the dispatch of the summary reports.
The convocation of the members of the General Council must state the date, the place and the agenda.
The session of the Executive Committee in the year in which the General Council sits must be held 45 days beforehand.
At each session of the General Council, draft internal regulations are submitted to the assessment of the members.

The General Council sits validly if 3/4 of its members are present.
Its decisions are taken by a 2/3 majority.
The General Council itself determines the method of financing its programme of action.

In order better to fulfil its mission as the organ of material development of the association, the General Council may initiate studies on certain projects of major interest in the various fields of intervention of the Church.
During the sittings of the General Council, guests may participate and give opinions without having the right to vote.
The purpose, composition, powers and functioning of the Assembly of Apostles are defined in articles 55 to 59 of the Statutes.
In addition to its functioning as defined in articles 60 to 63 of the statutes, the regulatory provisions of the General Council apply mutatis mutandis to the Assembly.
The purpose, composition, powers and functioning of the Constituent Assembly are defined in articles 60 to 63 of the Statutes.
The purpose, composition, powers and functioning of the Executive Committee are defined in articles 67 to 69 of the Statutes.
The purpose, composition, powers and functioning of the Provincial Council are defined in articles 70 to 72 of the Statutes.

The ecclesiastical province of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) is not the administrative province.
It may be a grouping of 2 or 3 administrative provinces, delimited by the Executive Committee and supervised by a consecrated Apostle, called the Provincial Apostle.
The ecclesiastical province is administered by a Provincial Office.

The Provincial Office is composed of:
• The Provincial Apostle
• The Deputy Provincial Apostle
• The Provincial Secretary
• The Provincial President of the Laity
• The Provincial President of the AFEBNM
• The Provincial Leader of the JEBNM.
• The Provincial Head of the PGM.
The Provincial Apostle is appointed for a renewable term of 4 years.

The Deputy Provincial Apostle works with the incumbent, whom he replaces when the latter is unable to act.
Under the supervision of the incumbent, the Deputy Provincial Apostle is in charge of cultural activities, the checking of membership cards, social assistance, demography and other matters.
The Provincial President of the Laity is in charge of the material development of the province under the supervision of the Provincial Apostle.
The Provincial Secretary is responsible for the secretariat and the accounts of the province under the supervision of the Provincial Apostle.

The provincial secretariat is composed of:
• The Provincial Secretary
• A cashier and
• A data-entry operator.

The Provincial Leader of the youth of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC), abbreviated JEBNM, the President of the Action de la Femme de l'Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC), abbreviated AFEBNM, and the Provincial Head of the PGM are in charge, respectively, of the guidance of the youth, of the mothers and of the Music, under the supervision of the Provincial Apostle.

All the members of the Provincial Office report directly to the Provincial Apostle.
Nevertheless, each of them may be approached directly by the Legal Representation, under the supervision of the Spiritual Head.

The Provincial Council is the spiritual organ of the province.
It is composed of the Provincial Apostle, all the consecrated Apostles of the province and the Provincial Deaconess of the AFEBNM.

The Provincial Council meets once a year in ordinary session.
At each session of the Provincial Council, the Provincial Apostle sends an invitation to the Spiritual Head who, where appropriate, may delegate a Representative to the sittings.
Three months before the holding of the session of the Provincial Council, the basic entities must send their report to the Provincial Office.
If the Spiritual Head has not taken part in the session, the Minutes must be submitted to his assessment before the decisions taken are executed.
The assembly elects the first and second rapporteur secretaries.

A quorum of 3/4 is required for the Assembly to be validly held.
Decisions are taken by simple majority.
The Minutes of the sessions are sent to the Supremacy via the Legal Representation and may be sent to the basic entities.

After consulting the Spiritual Head, the Provincial Council appoints the heads of the entities and those of the specialized services who have met the following criteria:
a) Be of good repute
b) Be a leader of men c) Have a spirit of initiative
d) Be a unifier
e) Have at least post-secondary education or equivalent
f) Enjoy good health g) Be competent in the specific field.
h) Have a clean financial record.

To be designated Provincial Apostle, one must:
a) Be a consecrated Apostle
b) Have led a parish for at least 10 years;
c) Hold at least a graduat (undergraduate diploma) or equivalent
d) Have a clean record
e) Have completed at least 10 years of apostolate.

To be Provincial Secretary, one must:
a) Be at least a preacher
b) Have a proven intellectual level
c) Be available
d) Have knowledge in the fields of computing, accounting and secretarial work
e) Obtain a favourable opinion from the Parish Council.

To be designated Provincial President of a specialized service, one must:
a) Be at least a preacher or a deaconess
b) Have a proven intellectual level
c) Be available
d) Be competent in the field concerned
e) Obtain a favourable opinion from the Parish Council
f) Have the capacity for design and planning.
The purpose, composition, powers and functioning of the Provincial Committee are defined in articles 73 to 75 of the statutes.

During the session, the Provincial Committee may be assisted by guests invited for the occasion, who are:
a) The Heads of the entities
b) Experts
c) Consultants, etc.
Guests do not have the right to vote.
Decisions are taken by simple majority.

The lines of material development whose examination falls within the competence of the Provincial Committee are in particular:
a) Construction: School, Temple, Office, Guest house, Medical facilities...
b) The creation of self-financing activities;
c) Acquisitions: concession, plot of land, vehicles and communication equipment.
The Provincial Committee draws up the inventory and ensures the protection of the patrimony of the Church in the Province.

Every movable and immovable asset belonging to the Church must have a file drawn up in three copies, one of which is kept at the Parish, one at the province and the original at the Legal Representation.
For the Mother Church, the original is kept at the Supremacy.
Through the Provincial Apostle, the Provincial Committee has the programme laid down by the General Assembly carried out.
At the beginning of the session of the Provincial Committee, the Provincial Apostle draws up a report on the results of the previous financial year as well as the prospects for the future.

The activity reports on material matters addressed to the Provincial Apostle shall be processed by the Provincial President of the Laity, who shall also draft the opening speech of the session of the Provincial Committee.
Forty-five days before the session of the Provincial Committee, the Provincial Office must meet to prepare the session.

One month before the holding of the session of the Provincial Committee, the Provincial Apostle notifies the members.
The notification must include the date, time, place and draft agenda of the session.
The Provincial Committee sits validly if 3/4 of its members are present.
The Provincial Committee may initiate studies on certain projects of major interest in the various lines of material development of the Province.

To be designated Provincial President of the Laity, one must:
a) Have been at least President of the Parish Committee,
b) Be competent in the field of the development of the Church,
c) Be a preacher,
d) Have significant professional experience in development,
e) Be available,
f) Have a university level of education or equivalent,
g) Obtain a favourable opinion from the Parish Council,
h) Be a leader of men, i) Have a clean financial record.
These conditions are cumulative.
The Urban/Provincial President of the Laity is appointed for a renewable term of 4 years.

For his activities, the Urban/Provincial President of the Laity must maintain a planning office composed of:
a) Secretary
b) A treasurer
c) One or two advisers
d) A project designer.

The Council of Apostles of the Extensions functions mutatis mutandis in the same way as the Assembly of Apostles of the Mother Church as defined by articles 55 to 59 of the Statutes and 104 to 105 of these Regulations.

The National Committee of the Branches functions mutatis mutandis in the same way as the General Assembly of the Mother Church as defined by articles 60 to 66 of the Statutes and 106 of these Regulations.

The Constituent Assembly of the Branches functions mutatis mutandis in the same way as the Constituent Assembly of the Mother Church as defined by articles 64 to 66 of the Statutes and 107 to 108 of these Regulations.

The National Executive Committee of the Branches functions mutatis mutandis in the same way as the Executive Committee of the Mother Church as defined by articles 67 to 69 of the Statutes and 1[...] of these Regulations.
The composition, powers and sittings of the Parish Council are defined in articles 76 to 78 of the Statutes.

The parish has two organs:
a) The Parish Council,
b) The Parish Committee.
The parish is directed by the Parish Council. However, the Parish Committee deals only with the management of material matters.
The parish is an ecclesiastical district whose geographical extent is fixed at its proclamation.

The parish is the basic cell and the centre of preaching of the Word of the Eternal.
It is the crucible of spiritual and social development.
The parish must have an e-mail address.

The parish is composed of sections subdivided into sub-sections.
The organization and functioning of sections and sub-sections are defined in the leaders' vade mecum.
The name of a parish is taken from the patrimony of the Church or from its geographical location (avenue, quarter...).
Each year, the Parish Committee and the heads of the specialized services of the parish send an activity report to the Provincial Apostle.

Administratively, the parish is governed by an office composed of the:
a) Head of Parish
b) Deputy Head of Parish
c) Parish Secretary
d) President of the Parish Committee
e) Youth Leader
f) Deaconess in charge of the parish
g) Worship Leader.

The Head of Parish is appointed for an indefinite term. Nevertheless, he may be transferred when necessary.
In case of abuse, he may be dismissed.
The Provincial Council draws up the staffing arrangement to be submitted for the approval of the Legal Representative.

The Head of Parish represents the Spiritual Head in his entity and reports hierarchically to the Provincial Apostle.
He is the head of all the organs of the parish.

The Head of Parish presides over the Parish Council and ensures:
a) The application of the doctrine of the Church
b) Respect for ecclesiastical discipline
c) The spiritual as well as material development of the parish
d) The doctrinal training of servants and members.
This list is not exhaustive.

The Head of Parish ensures the application of the doctrine by:
a) Teaching the doctrinal principles
b) Organizing recitation sessions c) Verifying the assimilation of the doctrinal principles and of the liturgical prayers
d) Following the content of the servants' preaching
e) Inquiring into the conduct of the members.
This list is not exhaustive.
The Head of Parish may have recourse to the intellectual or technical skills of one of his collaborators where needed in the general interest.
The Head of Parish may, by written proxy, delegate part of his powers to his deputy.

SRE DE LE The Head of Parish and his deputy are appointed by the Provincial Apostle on the proposal of the Provincial Council during an ordinary or extraordinary meeting and after consulting the Legal Representative.
For the Mother Church, the opinion is given by the Spiritual Head.

The Deputy Head of Parish works with the incumbent, whom he replaces when the latter is unable to act. He is responsible for:
a) Socio-cultural activities,
b) Checking membership cards,
c) The guidance of neophytes,
d) Assisting the parish secretary in the filing and organization of the parish office,
e) Keeping the registers of First Anointing, marriage and blessing of children,
f) Monitoring the calendar of programmes and of major operations,
g) Social assistance.
The President of the Parish Committee is responsible for the material development of the parish under the supervision of the Head of Parish.

The parish Youth Leader and the Deaconess in charge of the parish are responsible, respectively, for the guidance of the young people and of the mothers, under the supervision of the Head of Parish, Worship Leader.
The Parish Council meets once a month in ordinary session.

The Parish Council must:
• Organize training sessions on the doctrine for the benefit of members and servants.
• Watch out for any form of deviationist tendencies within the parish.
As regards the programme for the propagation of the Holy Word of the Eternal God, the parish office draws up the draft to be submitted to the assessment of the Parish Council.
The Parish Council also sits for the remuneration of members and servants.
The meetings of the Parish Council must be held at the seat of the parish, outside the sabbath day.

The agenda of the Parish Council must be prepared by the parish office.
For ordinary meetings, the members of the Parish Council must be informed by a letter specifying the date, the time and the agenda.

The decisions of the Parish Council are taken in accordance with the holy scriptures and the texts governing the life of the Church.
Two copies of the minutes of the meetings of the Parish Council are sent to the Provincial Apostle, who forwards one of them to the Supremacy via the Legal Representation.

In the event of indiscretion by one of its members, the Parish Council may expel him from this organ or suspend him from it, or else draw up a corresponding report for the assessment of the hierarchy.
If it is the president himself who is at fault, a member of the Parish Council may refer the matter to the Provincial Council, once the evidence has been gathered.
An adherent may be placed under discipline only when the evidence has been gathered (concordant testimonies or material evidence).

With the exception of the penalties of withdrawal of title, removal from office and excommunication, which fall within the competence of the Supremacy, disciplinary sanctions (warning, reprimand, suspension from duties, temporary prohibition from the sacraments) are pronounced by the authorities and organs designated in the table of the regulations.
• For an adherent: the Head of section or sub-section, the Head of Parish, then the Parish Council.
• For a servant: the Head of Parish, the Provincial Apostle, the Provincial Council, the Parish Council, the Assembly of Apostles or the Supremacy, depending on the sanction.
(Simplified table: see the original for details.)
Any adherent whose First Anointing card and membership card are not in order may not be promoted to the rank of servant, even if he meets the criteria.
No parish may use a servant who is not provided with his letter of testimony issued by his parish of origin.

The file of a servant must include the letter of transfer, his First Anointing card, his membership card, the information sheet, the marriage certificate for a married person, and the letter of promotion.

The Church recognizes only monogamous marriage between two persons of different sexes.
Divorce and mixed marriage may not be encouraged.
There is mixed marriage where there is no spiritual bond.
Marriage with a minor child is not tolerated, save for any exception provided by law.

For the promotion of servants, the criteria established by the Assembly of Apostles for each category must be scrupulously respected:
• An aspiring Disciple is promoted to Disciple after one year of observation. If, during the trial period, his conduct has not been satisfactory, the trial or observation period may be renewed for one more year.
A Disciple may be promoted to Preacher after completing 5 years.
• A Preacher may be promoted to Apostle after completing 5 years; merit is indispensable.
• The Pontificate falls under the Spiritual Head.
With the exception of the Spiritual Head, only the Parish Council may, after deliberation, carry out the promotion of servants.
Every servant must have a file at the parish office, at the provincial office and at the Legal Representation.
A servant who does not have a complete file at the Legal Representation may receive neither promotion nor testimony in the event of transfer to another country.
The file of a promoted servant must be forwarded within 30 days following his appointment.

Any indiscretion observed on the part of a member relating to the secrecy of the deliberations of the Parish Council or of the Purification is liable to removal from office if the evidence is established.
The removal from office of a servant must be requested from the Supremacy by a letter signed by the president of the Parish Council and attached to the Minutes of the Parish Council.

The cases not falling within the competence of the Parish Council, which must be submitted to the assessment of the Provincial Council after hearing the persons concerned and assessment, are:
• Abortion, poisoning, murder, assassination, rape...
• Divorce,
• Consulting soothsayers, fetishists and the dead.
• Misconduct committed by the Head of Parish or an Apostle...
The composition, powers and sittings of the Parish Committee are defined in articles 79 to 80 of the Statutes.
A member of the Parish Committee must be capable of making suggestions and possess a certain technical skill in one of the fields of interest to the development of the parish.

The 9 members of the Parish Committee are elected by direct suffrage in the course of [a meeting] of all the parishioners.
> The president of the organ is chosen by the Parish Council from among the elected members. *.

In the event of incapacity or abuse on the part of the President of the Parish Committee, 3/4 of the members of the Committee may demand his replacement.
The incompetence or inertia of a Parish Committee may prompt the Head of Parish to revitalize it.
Upon a written and reasoned request from the President, the Head of Parish may relieve and replace a member of the Committee before the end of the term of office.
The Parish Committee as an organ may be dissolved only by the Provincial Council on a reasoned proposal from the Provincial Committee.

The minutes of the meetings of the Parish Committee are drawn up in four copies, three of which are sent to the parish. The parish sends two copies to the Provincial Office, which forwards one of them to the Legal Representation.
For the Mother Church, the Supremacy receives the minutes in the last instance.
At least once a month, the Parish Committee gives the parishioners a detailed report of its activities.
As an organ, the Parish Committee works under the supervision of the Head of Parish. However, the latter may in no case substitute himself for the Parish Committee.
The President of the Parish Committee must maintain close relations and sincere collaboration with the Head of Parish.
Before being executed, the decisions of the Parish Committee are examined collegially with the Parish Council.
The Parish Committee collaborates with the Provincial Committee through the Provincial President of the Laity.
The President of the Parish Committee is required to send, at the end of each [...], an activity report to the Provincial President of the Laity through the [...] of the parish.

Four months before the holding of the session of the Provincial Committee, the President of the Parish Committee draws up a summary report of his activities, which he submits to the assessment of the Head of Parish for forwarding to the Provincial Apostle.

The Parish Committee must watch over the patrimony of the Church, in particular the regularization of land title documents, the payment of taxes, the protection of plots of land and of property and their maintenance, under the supervision of the Head of Parish.

To be a member of the Executive Committee, one must meet the following criteria:
A. General Criteria:
a) Be an effective member
b) Show fidelity to the doctrine and discipline of the Church
c) Have professional experience
d) Be available and obedient
e) Enjoy good mental health
f) Have a clean record (not having incurred a suspension at any rank whatsoever), save where the Supremacy decides otherwise.
g) Have skills specific to the functions indicated
h) Have a seniority of at least 10 years within the Church.
B. Specific Criteria.

To be Legal Representative or Deputy Legal Representative, one must:
a) Be a consecrated Apostle
b) Be elected by the electoral assembly or have been designated by the Prophet;
c) Hold at least a Licence (degree) in Theology or equivalent training.

To be Administrative Secretary, one must:
a) Be a consecrated Apostle
b) Hold a licence (degree) or equivalent qualification c) Have proven professional experience.
In the exercise of his functions, the Administrative Secretary is assisted by an assistant with the rank of Director.

The Assistant to the Administrative Secretary must have:
a) A university education and knowledge of executive secretarial work
b) At least the rank of preacher
c) A sense of organization
d) Proven professional experience.

To be Financial Director, one must:
a) Be an Apostle or a preacher
b) Have a university education or equivalent in financial management and/or accounting;
c) Proven professional experience.
The Provincial Apostles who are effective members are Members of the Executive Committee as defined by the Statutes in their article 68.
Any person who has committed serious misconduct in the exercise of his functions, or a breach entailing forfeiture of spiritual functions, is dismissed.
The physical or mental incapacity of a member of the Executive Committee must be confirmed by a medical report drawn up by three medical specialists.
In the event of absence or inability to act, the Legal Representative shall issue a proxy in favour of the Deputy to represent the Association.

The Proxy issued by the Legal Representative shall comprise:
a) The undersigned (the principal)
b) The reason
c) The duration
d) The extent of the powers.
The said proxy must be written on the Association's letterhead and bear its seal.
The Deputy Legal Representative performs any task entrusted to him by the Legal Representative, whom he assists in the exercise of his functions.

In the event of unforeseeable and/or permanent incapacity of the Legal Representative, the Deputy Legal Representative may not:
a) Perform acts of disposition,
b) Dismiss or hire staff,
c) Make transfers or exchanges of posts.
This applies until the installation of the Legal Representative chosen by the electoral Assembly.
The Legal Adviser is the Counsel (lawyer) of the Church.
In the exercise of his functions, the Legal Adviser must be instructed by the Legal Representative.
For any problem, the Legal Adviser must first submit the procedure to be followed to the assessment of the Legal Representative.

As the lawyer of the Church, the Legal Adviser must hold a special power of attorney signed by the Legal Representative for all acts to be performed.
He has the obligation to report regularly on the acts performed and to hand over to the Church the closed or filed case file.
All costs relating to the handling of the court case are borne by the Church.
Before his engagement, the Legal Adviser must have provided proof of his competence in handling the Church's cases.

In the event of a conflict, the local leader must inform the Legal Representative for all necessary measures.
IV. Administrative and Financial Management at Local Level —_ "er administrative and financial at Local Level and at the level of the Extension.
In towns or centres where there is more than one parish, only the Leader designated by the Spiritual Head shall have the power to represent the Church before the State or third parties.

The conditions for the appointment of a Head of an « Extension » are those relating to the Legal Representation of the Mother Church.
However, in the event of a shortage of trained officers, the Supremacy shall decide.
Any financial commitment to be made in the name of the Church towards third parties by a leader must obtain the opinion of the Supremacy before it is entered into.

The opening of a bank account at parish and provincial level must require the opinion of the Legal Representative.
For the Mother Church, the opinion is given by the Spiritual Head.

The Head of an « Extension » of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) is the Representative of the Head of the Church in the host country. In this capacity:
a) He commits and represents the Association before the State and before third parties
b) Ensures the establishment of KCCISME and watches over its orthodoxy in that country
c) Supervises the administrative, financial and material management of the whole Branch
d) Supports the development projects of the Mother Church
e) Provides for the needs of the Supremacy.

An Apostolic Delegate must:
a) Be a consecrated Apostle
b) Know the functioning of the Church
c) Have mastery of the doctrine of the Church
d) Have been head of a basic entity
e) Hold a university degree or equivalent.
The Apostolic Delegate serves as mentor to the Legal Representatives of the Extensions.
The Apostolic Delegate ensures the implementation of the instructions, guidelines and recommendations of the Supremacy in both the spiritual and material fields.

Assisted by 5 members in the exercise of his functions, the Apostolic Delegate is required to inform the Supremacy regularly through reports on the spiritual, material and financial management of the Church on the continent.

Except where there is no Apostolic Delegate, the Legal Representatives of the Extensions are required to make a regular report to the Apostolic Delegate on the activities relating to the life of the Church in their respective entities.

In the exercise of their respective functions, the Legal Representatives of the Extensions as well as the Apostolic Delegate must work in peace, fraternity and mutual respect in order to safeguard the dignity and unity of the Church in their host country.

The Legal Representatives of the Extensions and the Apostolic Delegate are relieved of their functions by the Supremacy in the event of objectively proven serious breaches.
A serious breach means any act contrary to the doctrine, the dignity and the unity of the Church.
The Legal Representatives must report regularly to the Spiritual Head on the spiritual, administrative, material and financial situation.
The Supremacy must ensure that the Legal Representatives are brought up to standard in all respects.
The whole Church owes obedience and submission to the Sovereign Pontiff.

The administrative, material and financial management of the Supremacy is carried out by staff designated by the Spiritual Head.
VI. Specialized services (LAITY-JEBNM-AFEBNM)
The laity brings together all non-consecrated members - men and women, boys and girls.

The Youth of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) brings together all young people, boys and girls, aged 0 to 25 years, for spiritual and social guidance as well as harmonious integration into society.
Any unmarried member is also considered a young person.
The Action de la Femme de l'Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) provides spiritual and social guidance to all the Women of the Church.
The organization and functioning of each specialized service are defined in a specific framework.

The Accounts of the Association comprise all the financial operations carried out [by the]:
Legal Representation.
However, each parish keeps its own accounts, the original of which it sends monthly to the Legal Representation.

The financial service of the Legal Representation comprises, in addition to the accounts department, the treasury, a central receipts cash office, a central disbursements cash office and an audit service.
The Financial System of the Extensions functions mutatis mutandis on the model of the Legal Representation of the Mother Church.
Every financial operation carried out at each level of the Church and in each structure must be recorded and communicated to the hierarchy by accounting mail.

In order to organize financial management efficiently and safeguard the life of the Church, a Financial Management Committee is established, composed of:
a) Financial Director
b) A Chief Accountant
c) A treasurer
d) A cashier
e) An accounting assistant
f) Two auditors.
The organization and functioning of the Financial Management Committee are defined in a Vade-mecum.

The Cheque and/or the cash disbursement voucher is signed by the following three persons:
a) The Legal Representative
b) The Financial Director c) The Administrative Secretary At the level of the Mother Church, only the Spiritual Head directs financial operations.
The annual Accounts accompanied by the accounting documents must be filed with the Supremacy no later than 31 January by the organs of the Extensions and of the Mother Church.
The amendment of the Statutes or of the Internal Regulations falls within the competence of the [...] effective members ruling by absolute majority.

The proposal of the Executive Committee for the amendment of the Statutes and of the Internal Regulations must be accompanied by an explanatory memorandum and by a draft of the statutes or of the Internal Regulations to be submitted to the deliberation of the effective members.
The Spiritual Head presides over the meeting of the Constituent Assembly at which the decision to amend the Statutes and/or the Internal Regulations is adopted.

The Minutes of the meeting of the effective members sitting for the amendment of the Statutes or of the Internal Regulations must be signed by the Spiritual Head and by the rapporteur chosen at the meeting.

The Statutes are enforceable against all after the opinion of the Spiritual Head and publication in the Official Journal through the Minister of Justice, in accordance with article 9 of Law n°004/2001 of 20 July 2001 laying down the general provisions applicable to non-profit associations and to public utility establishments.
The Internal Regulations are enforceable against all after the notarial deed.
On Dissolution.

The Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC) cannot be dissolved.
In the event of dissolution, reference shall be made to article 104 of the statutes.

In order to perpetuate the person of the Prophet and Visible Founder of the Eglise Bon Nouveau Message (KCC), His Eminence DIZOLELE-MPUNGU WAFIDUSWA Isaac, a philanthropic work called the « Fondation Son Eminence le Prophète DIZOLELE-MPUNGU WAFIDUSWA Isaac, Fondateur de l'EBNM » (His Eminence the Prophet DIZOLELE-MPUNGU WAFIDUSWA Isaac Foundation, Founder of the EBNM), which was created by him, is supported by the Church.
